handoff.purpose: Define ignore rules parsing and matching semantics for .daedalusignore files.

symbols.name: SCOPE_ALGO_SALT
symbols.note: Salt string for scope fingerprint to invalidate caches on algorithm change.

symbols.name: _Rule
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing a single ignore rule with pattern, negated, dir_only, anchored.

symbols.name: _parse_line
symbols.note: Parses a single line from .daedalusignore into a _Rule or None.

symbols.name: IgnoreRules
symbols.note: Ordered list of rules; last match wins. Provides matches() method.

claims.text: BUMP THIS whenever the scope changes what an index CONTAINS rather than which files it covers.

claims.text: The scope fingerprint is the index cache key, and it is built only from the center list and the ignore patterns -- so a change to the *interpretation* of an unchanged center (v2: Python dotted names became package-relative for files under a center root) leaves the key identical and every warm cache, in-process and on disk, keeps serving the OLD graph.
claims.why: Scope fingerprint and cache key logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Unscoped repos are unaffected: index._scope_key gives them a bare path key that never consults this fingerprint, so their cache is not invalidated.
claims.why: index._scope_key not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A pattern containing a slash is repo-root anchored, exactly as gitignore defines it: 'docs/vendor' means that path, not any directory named 'vendor' inside any 'docs'.
claims.why: Code on line 83: anchored = '/' in line or raw.lstrip().startswith('/') matches claim.

claims.text: Ordered rule list. Last match wins, so ! can carve exceptions.
claims.why: matches() method on lines 95-100 implements last-match-wins logic.

claims.text: True when repo-relative POSIX path rel is ignored. Last-match-wins, so ordering is load-bearing and callers must not reorder the file.
claims.why: matches() loop (lines 97-99) updates verdict per rule, so last rule wins.

claims.text: A directory rule matches every descendant, which is the only reason references/ covers references/a/b.py.
claims.why: Directory rule matching every descendant is not fully implemented in this chunk; _hit for anchored patterns has startswith check (line 109) but unanchored dir_only logic is missing.

observations.what: The _hit method for unanchored patterns is incomplete; it lacks handling for dir_only and '**' patterns.
The docstring claims about performance (1.9s parse vs 96% clone passes) are not backed by code in this chunk.
The _parse_line function strips leading '/' from patterns but the anchored flag is set based on raw line; this may lead to inconsistency if pattern starts with '/' and also contains a slash.
